skillSays: Design from fixed scales and never invent a value: a 4-8-12-16-24-32-48-64-96 spacing scale, a 12-72px type scale in px/rem, two font weights, five shadow elevations.
Build hierarchy with weight and colour instead of size: three text greys at most, one solid primary action, secondary as outline, tertiary as a link.
Use 8-10 grey shades and 5-10 shades per colour written in HSL, defined up front and never generated at runtime; flip contrast (dark text on a tint) instead of grey-on-colour.
Always put more space around a group than within it, shrink large elements faster than small ones on mobile, and give every functional border 3:1 contrast.
Never rely on colour alone: pair status colours with an icon or text, and put large icons inside coloured circles instead of scaling them up.

changes: Started from the skill's tokens.css and retuned the grey and primary ramps to a teal hue instead of picking colours ad hoc
Three-level button hierarchy in the hero: solid primary, outline secondary, underlined tertiary link
Feature icons sit in 48px tinted circles, and status chips pair colour with a check or clock icon
Real depth from a layered two-part shadow on the appointment card, with weight and grey shades doing the hierarchy rather than larger type
Clinic is emphasised by de-emphasising the others: outline buttons on Solo and Group, a solid primary and a stronger elevation on Clinic
Prices are large and bold while '/month' and 'Billed monthly' drop to tertiary grey, following 'emphasise by de-emphasising'
The toggle is a real switch with label text that changes weight, and the savings chip pairs green with text
Inputs are 44px with a 3:1 functional border (--border-strong) and a visible focus ring, separate from the decorative divider token
Errors use a red tint with dark red text and a circled icon, so colour is never the only signal, and help text is hidden while an error is shown
Spacing follows the scale throughout, with more space between fields than between a label and its input
